solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shipping area that's not included in Scottish TV?

definitions.text: Shipping area that's not included in Scottish TV?

parts.words: Shipping area that's not included in Scottish TV?
parts.note: a sea area of the shipping forecast, read playfully as a broadcaster that a Scottish viewer would not count among their own stations

explanation.surface: A puzzled viewer wonders which shipping-forecast region gets left out of Scotland's television coverage.
explanation.walkthrough: The sea between England and France is both a named shipping-forecast area and, taken literally, a TV station from south of the border: a channel that is English, so hardly Scottish TV.
explanation.definitionFit: The stretch of sea separating Britain from France is one of the named areas in the BBC shipping forecast.

clue.text: No nurse will release name of famous person?

indicators.note: release means to let a letter go from the word for nurse

parts.note: to nurse is to tend, look after

explanation.surface: A nurse refuses to let slip the name of a celebrity patient.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No' is used as it stands; 'will release' signals the letter for name coming out of the nurse word.
explanation.definitionFit: A noted person is well known and celebrated, so the adjective matches famous.

clue.text: It has end twirling to snare a steer's rear?

definitions.text: It has end twirling to snare a steer's rear?

indicators.note: to snare means the turned word catches the next letters inside it
twirling turns the word for end around, so it reads backwards

parts.note: the tail is the end of something

indicators.note: rear picks out the last letter of steer's

explanation.surface: A cowboy's rope, its end spinning, catches a bullock by the hindquarters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twirling' reverses TAIL to LIAT; 'to snare' puts A plus R ('rear' of steer's) inside it. The whole clue also describes the rope.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, a rope with a running noose that a cowboy twirls to catch cattle.

clue.text: Has cash register for sale? It's not shifting

parts.note: a shop that has goods for sale stocks them
a till is a shop's cash register

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper puts the till up for sale, but it isn't moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for sale' completes the sense of 'Has': to stock is to have something on sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock-still means completely motionless, so something described that way is not shifting at all.

clue.text: Point securing second in competition

indicators.note: securing means holding, so the competition word holds the letter inside

parts.note: a cup is a sporting competition, like the FA Cup

explanation.surface: Claiming second place in a contest earns a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'securing' puts S inside CUP.
explanation.definitionFit: A cusp is a pointed end, such as the tip of a crescent moon or a point on a tooth.

clue.text: Commend item for phone linked to travel

parts.note: an app is an application installed on a phone
to rove is to travel about

explanation.surface: A recommendation for a mobile app tied to journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: To approve of something is to speak well of it or endorse it, so commend fits.

clue.text: Portion of vegetarian diet? I for one will derive sustenance

indicators.note: for says I takes the place of the letter for one

parts.note: nuts are a staple of a vegetarian diet
a ration is a portion or allowance
A means one, as in 'a pound'

explanation.surface: A vegetarian wonders whether their helping is enough to keep them going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I for one' replaces the A in NUT RATION with I. 'I for one' reads like a speaker volunteering, but it is the substitution.
explanation.definitionFit: Nutrition is nourishment from food, which is what sustenance means.

clue.text: Novel backstage supremo?

definitions.meaning: a book by William Golding about schoolboys stranded on an island
the flies are the space above a theatre stage, so their lord would rule backstage

explanation.walkthrough: In a theatre the flies are the area above the stage where scenery is hung, so the lord of them is a jokey backstage boss.
explanation.definitionFit: William Golding's 1954 novel takes its title from a name for Beelzebub, and the theatre's flies supply the second sense.

clue.text: Working first with a current University to provide support services

indicators.note: working means the letters are worked over into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A university pairs its first job with a current one to keep services running.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Working' looks like it means employed, but it shuffles FIRST, A, CURRENT and U.
explanation.definitionFit: Infrastructure is the basic network of roads, power and utilities on which a society depends, its underlying support services.

clue.text: Ill-famed hunter almost caught by them?

indicators.note: caught by says the shortened hunter is held inside the letters for them

parts.note: them is the people who are not us, so the phrase NOT US stands for them

indicators.note: almost says the hunter's name is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: Orion is the hunter of Greek myth, also the constellation

explanation.surface: A disreputable hunter is nearly captured by some unnamed others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Them' is read as the people who are not us. Orion is the great hunter of Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ill-famed is widely known for something bad, which is exactly what being infamous or of bad repute means.

clue.text: Religious leader? Archbishop of Canterbury, say, covers it ultimately

indicators.note: covers means the peer wraps around the letter that follows

parts.note: the Archbishop of Canterbury sits in the House of Lords as one of the Lords Spiritual, so is an example of a peer

indicators.note: ultimately picks out the final letter of the word it

explanation.surface: The head of the Church of England is described as covering something up in the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes T from 'it', and 'covers' puts PEER around it. The Archbishop of Canterbury is a member of the House of Lords, the UK's upper chamber, so a peer.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Peter led the apostles and is counted as the first pope, so he is a religious leader; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Article in German inspired by this spider?

parts.words: Article in German inspired by this
parts.note: the answer split into a colour and a word for backwards tells you to read the colour right to left, which gives der, a German definite article

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature in German takes its inspiration from a particular spider.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, taken as an instruction, turns RED back into DER, a German word for the, so the clue words describe what the answer builds.
explanation.definitionFit: The redback is a venomous Australian spider, a close relative of the black widow, with a red stripe on its abdomen.

clue.text: Murder spy boss over feature of game?

parts.note: an order to murder M, the Bond spy chief, would be 'do M in'
O is the cricket abbreviation for over on a scorecard

explanation.surface: An instruction to kill the head of espionage, with the game element tacked on as a teaser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Murder spy boss' is read as a whole instruction, 'do M in', with M the head of the secret service in the James Bond stories.
explanation.definitionFit: A domino is one of the spotted tiles played in the game of dominoes, so it is a component of that game.

clue.text: Decline involving water power? It's not really an emergency

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the decline holds the water inside

parts.note: a fall is a decline
the sea is a body of water
an arm, as in 'the long arm of the law', is power or might

explanation.surface: Falling water levels and lost power alarm someone, though there's no real crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Power' is arm as in 'the long arm of the law'.
explanation.definitionFit: A false alarm is a warning given for a danger that turns out not to exist.

clue.text: Waves certainly moving trailing character on?

indicators.note: the trailing character is the word's last letter, and moving it on means advancing it one step through the alphabet

parts.note: sure, as in 'sure, I'll come', means certainly

explanation.surface: Waves are surely in motion, with something following behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving trailing character on' advances the final E of SURE to the next letter of the alphabet, F.
explanation.definitionFit: Surf is the mass of breaking waves rolling onto a shore, so the plural noun is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Kitchen worker not fully integrated into work routine in Kent town

indicators.note: integrated into places the shortened worker inside the rota

parts.note: a roster is a rota setting out who works when

indicators.note: not fully says the last letter of the kitchen worker is cut off

parts.note: a chef works in a kitchen

explanation.surface: A cook is only partly brought into the shift pattern in a Kentish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not fully' cuts the last letter from the kitchen worker; 'integrated into' places what is left in the rota. Kent is a county in south-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rochester is a historic cathedral city on the River Medway in Kent, south-east England.

clue.text: Planner is following version of target set in stone

indicators.note: set in says that combination is placed inside the abbreviation for stone

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British unit of weight of fourteen pounds

indicators.note: following puts the word is after the rearranged letters
version of says the word target appears in a new arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A planner sits after a target whose shape is carved in stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of' rearranges target to TRATEG; 'following' and 'set in' then place the pieces. Stone is a British unit of weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A strategist devises long-term plans and campaigns, so is a kind of planner.

clue.text: No opening for direct playing by top-ranked performer

indicators.note: playing, like a musician improvising, says the remaining letters are rearranged
no opening means the first letter of direct is removed

parts.note: the A-list is the top rank of celebrities

explanation.surface: A top-billed performer is denied the chance to conduct the playing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No opening for' drops D from DIRECT to leave IRECT; 'playing' rearranges that to RECIT, followed by A-LIST.
explanation.definitionFit: A recitalist gives solo recitals of music or poetry, so is a type of performer.

clue.text: Hear about old sad story

indicators.note: about means the word for hear goes round the word for old

parts.note: a judge will hear or try a case
aged means old

explanation.surface: Listen to an old, melancholy tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' is meant in the legal sense: a judge hears, or tries, a case. 'about' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedy is a drama or story with a sorrowful, often fatal ending.

clue.text: Eager to promote new joint

indicators.note: to promote means to move something up, here moving the letter for new earlier in the word

parts.note: keen means eager

explanation.surface: Someone keen to push a new joint venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to promote' lifts the N of KEEN from the end to second place.
explanation.definitionFit: The knee is the hinge joint between thigh and lower leg.

clue.text: Literary lion: poet, ultimately using oblique style?

parts.note: Aslan is the lion in C S Lewis's Narnia books

indicators.note: ultimately picks the final letter of poet

explanation.surface: A literary figure, poet in the end, writes in a roundabout manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literary lion' suggests a great writer, but here it is Narnia's lion; 'ultimately' gives T from 'poet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Aslant means at a slant or angle, so it describes something oblique.

clue.text: Former leader in the main returning aboard old chariot?

indicators.note: aboard puts the backward sea inside the vehicle

parts.note: a car, in older and poetic use, is a chariot

indicators.note: returning says the word for the main is written backwards

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the open sea

explanation.surface: A former leader heads back across the sea aboard an ancient chariot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the main round to give AES; 'aboard' is the container signal. 'Main' is a poetic word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Caesar led Rome before his assassination, and the title passed to later emperors.

clue.text: Ways artillerymen will make revolution in weaponry

indicators.note: a revolution is a turning round, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: lanes are roads or ways
RA is the Royal Artillery, the British Army's gunners

explanation.surface: Gunners plot a revolution armed with their stock of weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will make revolution' turns LANESRA round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An arsenal is a store or stock of weapons and ammunition, so it stands for a nation's weaponry.

clue.text: Contributor to luncheon — a chop or a chip

indicators.note: Contributor to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A list of what goes into lunch: a chop, or perhaps some chips.
explanation.definitionFit: A nacho is a tortilla chip, usually served topped with cheese.

clue.text: Long story, a thing to put you to sleep, on reflection

indicators.note: on reflection, as in a mirror, means the letters are read backwards

parts.words: thing to put you to sleep
parts.note: gas is the anaesthetic that puts a patient to sleep

explanation.surface: A long tale that, thinking it over, sends you to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns A GAS round. 'put you to sleep' hints at a boring story, but it is the anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A saga is a long, heroic story, originally an Icelandic or Norse prose epic.

clue.text: Dogged policeman letting second go free

indicators.note: letting a part go means removing it from the word

parts.note: the Mounties of Canada's police are famed for always getting their man, so dogged
a mo, as in 'wait a mo', is a moment or second

explanation.surface: A tenacious officer allows a second suspect to walk free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letting ... go' removes MO from MOUNTIE. The 'go' is the second half of that indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: To untie something is to loosen its knots and so set it free.

clue.text: Where a valley gets filled with one — Switzerland?

definitions.text: Where a valley gets filled with one — Switzerland?

indicators.note: gets filled with says the valley is packed out with the next pieces

parts.note: a vale is a valley
an means one, as in 'an apple'
CH is the international vehicle code for Switzerland

explanation.surface: Asking where a valley might be filled with snow, with Switzerland as the obvious place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets filled with' is the container signal. Read whole, the clue also describes a Swiss valley buried by a snowslide.
explanation.definitionFit: A mass of snow sliding down a mountainside fills the valley below, a hazard typical of the Swiss Alps.

clue.text: Vaguely monitor delay (about a year) in parliamentary process

indicators.note: about puts the monitor and delay letters around the article and year letter
vaguely says the combined letters are jumbled into no clear order

explanation.surface: Someone loosely keeping an eye on a hold-up that has lasted about a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps MONITOR DELAY round A and Y, and 'Vaguely' shuffles all fourteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In the UK House of Commons this is a motion tabled by MPs for debate on an unspecified day, used mainly to gather signatures.
